findings.title: Accent-derived variables now switch to `--primary`, which the description says this PR does not do
findings.body:
`AccentVars` declares the focus outline, expand/collapse icon colour, filter focus border, active grouping-toolbar border and selected-cell background again on the shadcn theme element. That makes `var(--infinite-accent-color)` resolve there, and on this theme it is `var(--primary)`. Before, these were resolved where the default theme declares them, so they were blue.

The PR description says these colours are "Not changed here" and are "left for a separate decision". It also says a light page on a light OS has "0 changed" variables. The new spec test asserts the opposite: these colours equal `--primary`.

What goes wrong: every existing shadcn-theme user sees a different focus outline, selection fill and expand icon, even in light mode. Either drop `AccentVars` (and its test), or update the description and changelog so the visual change is a deliberate, documented decision.

findings.title: Four mode-dependent variables keep their light values in dark mode
findings.body:
`MODE_DEPENDENT_VARS` pins 14 variables to the default theme's light values, and `ShadcnDarkVars` spreads `ShadcnLightVars` into the dark mode. The dark object then overrides only 10 of those 14. These four are never overridden:
- `GroupingToolbar.color`
- `GroupingToolbar.activeBackground`
- `GroupingToolbarItem.border`
- `GroupingToolbarItem.activeBackground`

In the default theme these four had dark values when the OS was dark. Now a dark page always gets the light ones (for example light-mode text colour, border and active background in the grouping toolbar), and the toolbar can be hard to read on a dark background.

I could not see the rest of `ShadcnLightVars` after line 76; if it maps these four to shadcn/ui variables, there is no bug. Otherwise, give them dark values here, for example `var(--foreground)`, `var(--muted)` and `1px solid var(--border)`.
